verses.text: God talk to Jacob say, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and dwell dere. Make one altar dere to God, wey appear to you when you flee from di face of Esau your brother.”
Den Jacob talk to im household, and to all wey dey with am, “Put away di foreign gods wey dey among una, purify una self, and change una clothes.
Make we arise, and go up to Bethel. I go make one altar dere to God, wey answer me for di day of my distress, and don dey with me for di way wey I go.”
Dem give Jacob all di foreign gods wey dey dem hand, and di rings wey dey dem ears. Jacob hide dem under di oak wey dey by Shechem.
Dem journey, and terror of God dey on di cities wey dey round dem, and dem no pursue di pikin dem of Jacob.
So Jacob come to Luz, wey dey di land of Canaan, wey na Bethel, e and all di people wey dey with am.
E build one altar dere, and call di place El Bethel, because dere God reveal imself to am, when e flee from di face of im brother.
Deborah, Rebekah nurse, die, and dem bury am below Bethel under di oak. Dem call im name Allon Bacuth.
God appear to Jacob again, when e come from Paddan Aram, and bless am.
God talk to am say, “Your name na Jacob. Dem no go call your name Jacob again, but Israel go be your name.” E call im name Israel.
God talk to am say, “I na God Almighty. Born plenty pikin and multiply. One nation and company of nations go come from you, and kings go come out of your body.
Di land wey I give Abraham and Isaac, I go give am to you, and to your seed after you I go give di land.”
God go up from am for di place wia e talk with am.
Jacob set up one pillar for di place wia e talk with am, one pillar of stone. E pour drink offering on top of am, and pour oil on top of am.
Jacob call di name of di place wia God talk with am, Bethel.
Dem journey from Bethel. Dem still dey some distance from Ephrath, when Rachel go into labour, and e get hard labour.
E come be say, when e dey hard labour, di midwife talk to am say, “No fear, because dis one too na pikin man wey you go get.”
E come be say, as im soul dey go out, because e dey die, e call im name Benoni, but im papa call am Benjamin.
Rachel die, and dem bury am for di way to Ephrath, wey na Bethlehem.
Jacob set up one pillar upon im grave. Dat na di pillar of Rachel grave to dis day.
Israel journey, and pitch im tent beyond di tower of Eder.
E come be say, when Israel dey dwell for dat land, Reuben go sleep with Bilhah, im papa concubine, and Israel hear am. Now Jacob pikin man dem na 12.
Di pikin dem of Leah: Reuben, Jacob firstborn, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
Di pikin dem of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
Di pikin dem of Bilhah, Rachel servant: Dan and Naphtali.
Di pikin dem of Zilpah, Leah servant: Gad and Asher. Dis na di pikin dem of Jacob, wey dem born to am for Paddan Aram.
Jacob come to Isaac im papa for Mamre, to Kiriath Arba, wey na Hebron, wia Abraham and Isaac stay as foreigners.
Di days of Isaac na 180 years.
Isaac die, and join im people, old and full of days. Esau and Jacob im pikin dem bury am.
Now dis na di generations of Esau, wey na Edom.
Esau take im wives from di pikin woman dem of Canaan: Adah, di pikin woman of Elon di Hittite; and Oholibamah, di pikin woman of Anah, di pikin woman of Zibeon di Hivite;
and Basemath, Ishmael pikin woman, di sister of Nebaioth.
Adah born to Esau Eliphaz. Basemath born Reuel.
Oholibamah born Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. Dis na di pikin dem of Esau, wey dem born to am for di land of Canaan.

Esau take im wives, im pikin man dem, im pikin woman dem, and all di persons of im house, im livestock, all im animals, and all im goods wey e get for di land of Canaan, and go to one land away from im brother Jacob.
Because dem riches too much to dwell together, and di land wia dem dey stay as foreigners no fit carry dem because of dem livestock.
Esau dwell for Mount Seir. Esau na Edom.
Dis na di generations of Esau, di papa of di Edomites, for Mount Seir.
Dis na di names of Esau pikin dem: Eliphaz, di pikin of Adah, Esau wife; Reuel, di pikin of Basemath, Esau wife.
Di pikin dem of Eliphaz na Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
Timna na concubine of Eliphaz, Esau pikin. E born Amalek to Eliphaz. Dis na di pikin dem of Adah, Esau wife.
Dis na di pikin dem of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. Dem na di pikin dem of Basemath, Esau wife.
Dis na di pikin dem of Oholibamah, di pikin woman of Anah, di pikin woman of Zibeon, Esau wife: e born to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
Dis na di chiefs of di pikin dem of Esau: di pikin dem of Eliphaz, di firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. Dis na di chiefs wey come from Eliphaz for di land of Edom. Dem na di pikin dem of Adah.
Dis na di pikin dem of Reuel, Esau pikin: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. Dis na di chiefs wey come from Reuel for di land of Edom. Dem na di pikin dem of Basemath, Esau wife.
Dis na di pikin dem of Oholibamah, Esau wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. Dis na di chiefs wey come from Oholibamah, di pikin woman of Anah, Esau wife.
Dis na di pikin dem of Esau, wey na Edom, and dis na dem chiefs.
Dis na di pikin dem of Seir di Horite, di inhabitants of di land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. Dis na di chiefs wey come from di Horites, di pikin dem of Seir, for di land of Edom.
Di pikin dem of Lotan na Hori and Heman. Lotan sister na Timna.
Di pikin dem of Shobal na Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
Dis na di pikin dem of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. Dis na Anah wey find di hot springs for di wilderness, as e dey feed di donkeys of Zibeon im papa.
Dis na di pikin dem of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah, di pikin woman of Anah.
Dis na di pikin dem of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
Dis na di pikin dem of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
Dis na di pikin dem of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
Dis na di chiefs wey come from di Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan. Dis na di chiefs wey come from di Horites, according to dem chiefs for di land of Seir.
Dis na di kings wey reign for di land of Edom, before any king reign over di pikin dem of Israel.
Bela di pikin of Beor reign for Edom. Di name of im city na Dinhabah.
Bela die, and Jobab di pikin of Zerah of Bozrah reign for im place.
Jobab die, and Husham of di land of di Temanites reign for im place.
Husham die, and Hadad di pikin of Bedad, wey strike Midian for di field of Moab, reign for im place. Di name of im city na Avith.
Hadad die, and Samlah of Masrekah reign for im place.
Samlah die, and Shaul of Rehoboth by di River reign for im place.
Shaul die, and Baal Hanan di pikin of Achbor reign for im place.
Baal Hanan di pikin of Achbor die, and Hadar reign for im place. Di name of im city na Pau. Im wife name na Mehetabel, di pikin woman of Matred, di pikin woman of Mezahab.
Dis na di names of di chiefs wey come from Esau, according to dem families, after dem places, by dem names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram. Dis na di chiefs of Edom, according to dem dwelling places for di land of dem possession. Dis na Esau, di papa of di Edomites.
Jacob dwell for di land wia im papa stay as foreigner, for di land of Canaan.

Dis na di generations of Jacob. Joseph, wey dey 17 years old, dey feed di flock with im brothers. E dey young with di pikin dem of Bilhah and di pikin dem of Zilpah, im papa wives. Joseph bring bad report of dem to dem papa.
Now Israel love Joseph pass all im pikin dem, because e na pikin of im old age, and e make am one coat of many colors.
Im brothers see say dem papa love am pass all im brothers, and dem hate am, and dem no fit talk peacefully to am.
Joseph dream one dream, and e tell am to im brothers, and dem hate am more.
E talk to dem say, “Hear dis dream wey I don dream.
Look, we dey bind sheaves for di field, and look, my sheaf rise up, and stand upright. Look, una sheaves gather round, and bow down to my sheaf.”
Im brothers talk to am say, “You go really reign over us? You go really rule over us?” Dem hate am more for im dreams and for im words.
E dream another dream, and tell am to im brothers, talk say, “Look, I don dream another dream: and look, di sun, di moon, and 11 stars dey bow down to me.”
E tell am to im papa and to im brothers. Im papa rebuke am, talk to am say, “Wetin be dis dream wey you don dream? Me and your mama and your brothers go really come bow down to di ground before you?”
Im brothers envy am, but im papa keep di saying for mind.
Im brothers go to feed dem papa flock for Shechem.
Israel talk to Joseph say, “Your brothers dey feed di flock for Shechem. Come, make I send you to dem.” E talk to am say, “Here I dey.”
E talk to am say, “Go now, see if e dey well with your brothers, and well with di flock, and bring me word again.” So e send am out of di valley of Hebron, and e come to Shechem.
One man find am, and look, e dey wander for di field. Di man ask am say, “Wetin you dey look for?”
E talk say, “I dey look for my brothers. Tell me, wia dem dey feed di flock?”
Di man talk say, “Dem don go from here, because I hear dem talk say, ‘Make we go to Dothan.’” Joseph go after im brothers, and find dem for Dothan.
Dem see am afar off, and before e come near to dem, dem plan against am to kill am.
Dem talk to each other say, “Look, dis dreamer dey come.
Come now therefore, make we kill am, and throw am into one of di pits, and we go talk say wild animal don devour am. We go see wetin go happen to im dreams.”
Reuben hear am, and deliver am out of dem hand, talk say, “Make we no kill am.”
Reuben talk to dem say, “Una no shed blood. Throw am into dis pit wey dey for di wilderness, but lay no hand on am,” so that e go deliver am out of dem hand, to restore am to im papa.
E come be say, when Joseph come to im brothers, dem strip Joseph of im coat, di coat of many colors wey dey on am,
and dem take am, and throw am into di pit. Di pit empty. No water dey inside.

Dem sit down to eat bread, and dem lift up dem eyes and look, and look, one caravan of Ishmaelites dey come from Gilead, with dem camels bearing spices, balm, and myrrh, dey go carry am down to Egypt.
Judah talk to im brothers say, “Wetin we go gain if we kill our brother and hide im blood?
Come, make we sell am to di Ishmaelites, and make our hand no dey on am, because na our brother and our flesh.” Im brothers listen to am.
Den Midianites, merchants, pass by, and dem draw and lift Joseph up out of di pit, and sell Joseph to di Ishmaelites for 20 pieces of silver. Dem bring Joseph into Egypt.
Reuben return to di pit, and look, Joseph no dey inside di pit, and e tear im clothes.
E return to im brothers, and talk say, “Di boy no dey. I, wia I go go?”
Dem take Joseph coat, kill one male goat, and dip di coat for di blood.
Dem send di coat of many colors, and dem bring am to dem papa, and talk say, “Dis one we don find. Examine am now, whether na your pikin coat or no.”
E recognize am, and talk say, “Na my pikin coat. Wild animal don devour am. Joseph surely don tear to pieces.”
Jacob tear im clothes, put sackcloth on im waist, and mourn for im pikin plenty days.
All im pikin man dem and all im pikin woman dem rise up to comfort am, but e refuse to dey comforted. E talk say, “No, I go go down to Sheol to my pikin mourning.” Im papa weep for am.
Di Midianites sell am into Egypt to Potiphar, one officer of Pharaoh, di captain of di guard.
E come be say for dat time, Judah go down from im brothers, and turn in to one Adullamite man, wey im name na Hirah.
Judah see dere di pikin woman of one Canaanite man wey im name na Shua. E take am, and go in to am.
E become pregnant, and born one pikin man, and e call im name Er.
E become pregnant again, and born one pikin man, and e call im name Onan.
E born another pikin man again, and call im name Shelah. Judah dey Chezib when e born am.
Judah take wife for Er im firstborn, wey im name na Tamar.
Er, Judah firstborn, wicked for di sight of di Lord, and di Lord kill am.
Judah talk to Onan say, “Go in to your brother wife, do di duty of husband brother to am, and raise up seed for your brother.”
Onan know say di seed no go be im own, and when e go in to im brother wife, e spill am for di ground, so that e no go give seed to im brother.
Di thing wey e do dey evil for di sight of di Lord, and e kill am too.

Den Judah talk to Tamar im pikin wife say, “Dwell as widow for your papa house, until Shelah my pikin don grow up,” because e talk say, “Make e no die too, like im brothers.” Tamar go and dwell for im papa house.
After plenty days, di pikin woman of Shua, Judah wife, die. Judah comfort imself, and e go up to im sheep shearers to Timnah, e and im friend Hirah di Adullamite.
Dem tell Tamar say, “Look, your husband papa dey go up to Timnah to shear im sheep.”

E take off di garments of im widowhood, cover imself with veil, wrap imself, and sit for di entrance to Enaim, wey dey di way to Timnah, because e see say Shelah don grow up, and dem no give am to am for wife.
When Judah see am, e think say e na prostitute, because e don cover im face.
E turn to am by di way, talk say, “Come now, make I come in to you,” because e no know say na im pikin wife. E talk say, “Wetin you go give me, so that you go come in to me?”
E talk say, “I go send you one young goat from di flock.” E talk say, “You go give me pledge, until you send am?”
E talk say, “Wetin pledge I go give you?” E talk say, “Your signet and your cord, and your staff wey dey your hand.” E give am dem, and go in to am, and e become pregnant by am.
E rise up, go im way, take off im veil, and put on di garments of im widowhood.
Judah send di young goat by di hand of im friend di Adullamite, to receive di pledge from di woman hand, but e no find am.
Den e ask di men of dat place say, “Wia di prostitute dey, wey dey Enaim by di wayside?” Dem talk say, “Prostitute no dey here.”
E return to Judah, and talk say, “I no find am. Di men of di place talk too say, ‘Prostitute no dey here.’”
Judah talk say, “Make e take am for imself, so that we no go dey shamed. Look, I send dis young goat, and you no find am.”

E come be say about three months later, dem tell Judah say, “Tamar your pikin wife don play di prostitute. Moreover, look, e dey pregnant by whoredom.” Judah talk say, “Bring am out, and make dem burn am.”
When dem bring am out, e send to Judah say, “Na di man wey own dis things make me pregnant.” E talk say, “Look well, whose be dis signet, dis cords, and dis staff.”
Judah recognize dem, and talk say, “E dey more righteous pass me, because I no give am to Shelah my pikin.” E no know am again.
E come be say for di time of im labour, look, twins dey im womb.
E come be say, when e dey labour, one put out im hand, and di midwife take scarlet thread, tie am for im hand, talk say, “Dis one come out first.”
E come be say, as e draw back im hand, look, im brother come out, and e talk say, “Why you don break out? Dis breach dey on you!” Na why dem call im name Perez.
After dat im brother come out, wey get di scarlet thread for im hand, and dem call im name Zerah.
Dem bring Joseph down to Egypt. Potiphar, one officer of Pharaoh, di captain of di guard, one Egyptian, buy am from di hand of di Ishmaelites wey bring am down dere.
Di Lord dey with Joseph, and e become prosperous man. E dey for im oga di Egyptian house.
Im oga see say di Lord dey with am, and say di Lord dey make all wey e do prosper for im hand.
Joseph find favour for im sight, and e serve am. E make am overseer over im house, and all wey e get e put for im hand.

E come be say from di time wey e make am overseer for im house, and over all wey e get, di Lord bless di Egyptian house for Joseph sake. Di Lord blessing dey on all wey e get, for di house and for di field.
E leave all wey e get for Joseph hand. E no know anything wey dey with am, except di bread wey e dey eat. Joseph handsome and fine to look at.
E come be say after dis things, im oga wife lift up im eyes to Joseph, and talk say, “Lie with me.”
But e refuse, and talk to im oga wife, “Look, my oga no know wetin dey with me for di house, and e don commit all wey e get to my hand.
Nobody pass me for dis house. E no hold back anything from me except you, because you na im wife. How then I go do dis great wickedness, and sin against God?”
E come be say as im oga wife dey talk to Joseph day by day, e no listen to am, to lie by am, or to dey with am.
E come be say about dis time, Joseph go into di house to do im work, and none of di men of di house dey inside.
Di woman catch am by im garment, talk say, “Lie with me.” E leave im garment for di woman hand, run, and go out.
E come be say, when di woman see say e don leave im garment for im hand, and run out,
di woman call di men of im house, talk to dem say, “See, e don bring Hebrew come to us to mock us. E come in to me to lie with me, and I cry with loud voice.
E come be say, when e hear say I lift up my voice and cry, e leave im garment by me, run, and go out.”
Di woman put im garment by am until im oga come home.
Di woman talk to am according to dis words, say, “Di Hebrew servant, wey you bring to us, come in to me to mock me,
and e come be say as I lift up my voice and cry, e leave im garment by me, and run out.”
E come be say, when im oga hear di words of im wife, wey e talk to am, say, “Dis na how your servant do me,” im anger burn.
Joseph oga take am, and put am for di prison, di place wia di king prisoners dey bound, and e dey there for di prison.
But di Lord dey with Joseph, show am kindness, and give am favour for di sight of di keeper of di prison.
Di keeper of di prison commit to Joseph hand all di prisoners wey dey di prison. Whatever dem do dere, na im dey do am.
Di keeper of di prison no look to anything wey dey im hand, because di Lord dey with am, and wetin e do, di Lord make am prosper.
E come be say after dis things, di butler of di king of Egypt and im baker offend dem oga di king of Egypt.
Pharaoh vex against im two officers, against di chief of di butlers, and against di chief of di bakers.
E put dem for custody for di house of di captain of di guard, into di prison, di place wia Joseph dey bound.
Di captain of di guard appoint Joseph with dem, and e serve dem. Dem stay for custody some time.
Di butler and di baker of di king of Egypt, wey dey bound for di prison, dream, di two of dem, each man im dream for one night, each man according to di interpretation of im dream.
Joseph come in to dem for morning, and see dem, and look, dem dey sad.
E ask Pharaoh officers wey dey with am for custody for im oga house, say, “Why una face dey sad today?”
Dem talk to am say, “We don dream one dream, and nobody dey to interpret am.” Joseph talk to dem say, “Interpretations no belong to God? Tell am to me now.”
Di chief butler tell im dream to Joseph, talk to am say, “For my dream, look, one vine dey before me,
and for di vine dey three branches. E be like say e bud, im blossoms shoot out, and im clusters ripen into grapes.
Pharaoh cup dey my hand. I take di grapes, press dem into Pharaoh cup, and give di cup into Pharaoh hand.”
Joseph talk to am say, “Dis na di interpretation of am: di three branches na three days.
Within three days Pharaoh go lift up your head, and restore you to your place. You go give Pharaoh im cup into im hand, as before, when you be im butler.
But remember me when e go well with you, and show kindness to me. Make you mention me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of dis house.
Because I don dey stolen away from di land of di Hebrews, and here too I no do anything wey dem for put me for di dungeon.”
When di chief baker see say di interpretation good, e talk to Joseph, “I too dey for my dream, and look, three baskets of white bread dey on my head.
For di uppermost basket dey all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and di birds dey eat dem out of di basket on my head.”
Joseph answer say, “Dis na di interpretation of am: di three baskets na three days.
Within three days Pharaoh go lift up your head from off you, and hang you on one tree, and di birds go eat your flesh from off you.”
E come be say for di third day, wey be Pharaoh birthday, e make feast for all im servants, and e lift up di head of di chief butler and di head of di chief baker among im servants.
E restore di chief butler to im butlership again, and e give di cup into Pharaoh hand,
but e hang di chief baker, as Joseph don interpret to dem.
Yet di chief butler no remember Joseph, but forget am.
E come be say at di end of two full years, Pharaoh dream, and look, e dey stand by di river.
Look, seven cows, fine to look at and fat, come up out of di river, and dem dey feed for di reed grass.
Look, seven other cows come up after dem out of di river, ugly and thin, and stand by di other cows for di bank of di river.
Di ugly and thin cows eat up di seven fine and fat cows. So Pharaoh wake.
E sleep and dream di second time, and look, seven ears of grain come up on one stalk, plump and good.
Look, seven ears, thin and scorched by di east wind, spring up after dem.
Di thin ears swallow up di seven plump and full ears. Pharaoh wake, and look, na dream.
E come be say for morning im spirit dey troubled, and e send and call all di magicians of Egypt and all di wise men. Pharaoh tell dem im dreams, but nobody fit interpret dem to Pharaoh.
Den di chief butler talk to Pharaoh say, “I dey remember my faults today.
Pharaoh vex with im servants, and put me for custody for di house of di captain of di guard, me and di chief baker.
We dream one dream for one night, me and am. We dream each man according to di interpretation of im dream.
One young Hebrew man dey with us dere, servant of di captain of di guard. We tell am, and e interpret our dreams to us. To each man according to im dream e interpret.
E come be say, as e interpret to us, so e happen. Pharaoh restore me to my office, and e hang am.”
Den Pharaoh send and call Joseph, and dem bring am quickly out of di dungeon. E shave imself, change im clothes, and come in to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh talk to Joseph say, “I don dream one dream, and nobody dey wey fit interpret am. I hear say about you, say when you hear dream, you fit interpret am.”
Joseph answer Pharaoh say, “E no dey for me. God go give Pharaoh answer of peace.”
Pharaoh talk to Joseph say, “For my dream, look, I dey stand on di bank of di river.
Look, seven cows, fat and fine to look at, come up out of di river, and dem dey feed for di reed grass.
Look, seven other cows come up after dem, poor, very ugly and thin, such as I no see for all di land of Egypt for ugliness.
Di thin and ugly cows eat up di first seven fat cows.
When dem don eat dem up, no one fit know say dem don eat dem, but dem still ugly as before. So I wake.
I see for my dream, and look, seven ears come up on one stalk, full and good.
Look, seven ears, withered, thin, and scorched by di east wind, spring up after dem.
Di thin ears swallow up di seven good ears. I tell am to di magicians, but nobody fit explain am to me.”
Joseph talk to Pharaoh say, “Pharaoh dream na one. God don declare to Pharaoh wetin e dey about to do.
Di seven good cows na seven years, and di seven good ears na seven years. Di dream na one.
Di seven thin and ugly cows wey come up after dem na seven years, and di seven empty ears scorched by di east wind go be seven years of famine.
Dis na di thing wey I talk to Pharaoh. God don show Pharaoh wetin e dey about to do.
Look, seven years of great plenty dey come for all di land of Egypt.
Seven years of famine go rise after dem, and all di plenty go dey forgotten for di land of Egypt. Di famine go consume di land.
Di plenty no go dey known for di land because of dat famine wey go follow, because e go be very grievous.
Di dream double to Pharaoh two times because di thing don dey established by God, and God go shortly bring am to pass.
Now therefore make Pharaoh look for one discreet and wise man, and set am over di land of Egypt.
Make Pharaoh do dis: make am appoint overseers over di land, and take di fifth part of di produce of di land of Egypt for di seven plenteous years.
Make dem gather all di food of dem good years wey dey come, and lay up grain under Pharaoh hand for food for di cities, and make dem keep am.
Di food go be for store for di land against di seven years of famine, wey go dey for di land of Egypt, so that di land no go perish through di famine.”
Di thing good for Pharaoh eyes, and for di eyes of all im servants.
Pharaoh talk to im servants say, “We fit find one like dis, man wey God Spirit dey inside?”
Pharaoh talk to Joseph say, “Since God don show you all dis, nobody dey wey get discretion and wisdom like you.
You go be over my house, and according to your word all my people go dey ruled. Only for di throne I go dey greater pass you.”
Pharaoh talk to Joseph say, “Look, I don set you over all di land of Egypt.”
Pharaoh take off im signet ring from im hand, and put am on Joseph hand, and clothe am with garments of fine linen, and put one gold chain about im neck.
E make am ride for im second chariot, and dem cry before am, “Bow di knee!” E set am over all di land of Egypt.
Pharaoh talk to Joseph say, “I na Pharaoh, and without you no man go lift up im hand or im foot for all di land of Egypt.”
Pharaoh call Joseph name Zaphenath Paneah. E give am Asenath, di pikin woman of Potiphera, priest of On, to be wife. Joseph go out over di land of Egypt.
Joseph dey 30 years old when e stand before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph go out from di presence of Pharaoh, and go through all di land of Egypt.
For di seven plenteous years di earth bring forth abundantly.
E gather up all di food of di seven years wey dey for di land of Egypt, and lay up di food for di cities. For every city e lay up di food of di fields wey surround am.
Joseph store up grain like di sand of di sea, plenty well well, until e stop to count, because e no fit count am.
Before di year of famine come, two pikin man dem born to Joseph, wey Asenath, di pikin woman of Potiphera, priest of On, born to am.
Joseph call di name of di firstborn Manasseh, say, “Because God don make me forget all my toil, and all my papa house.”
Di name of di second, e call Ephraim, say, “Because God don make me fruitful for di land of my affliction.”
Di seven years of plenty wey dey for di land of Egypt end.
Di seven years of famine begin to come, as Joseph don talk. Famine dey for all di lands, but for all di land of Egypt dey bread.
When all di land of Egypt famish, di people cry to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh talk to all di Egyptians say, “Go to Joseph. Wetin e talk to una, do am.”
Di famine dey over all di surface of di earth. Joseph open all di storehouses, and sell to di Egyptians. Di famine grow severe for di land of Egypt.
All di earth come to Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because di famine severe for all di earth.
